hypothesis: If fresh-water fish species are not shared between distant continents, almost no strictly freshwater fish species are native to two distant continents.
pass_criterion: Among native, strictly freshwater (non-diadromous, non-marine-tolerant) species in FishBase country checklists, fewer than 1% occur natively on two distant continents (e.g. Africa and South America), after removing introduced records.
fail_criterion: 10 or more such species, or 5% or more, are natively recorded on two distant continents. Results between the two thresholds are inconclusive.
interpretation: 'Distant continents' means continents separated by ocean (for example Africa and South America). 'Never' is operationalised as a rate under 1%, to allow taxonomic and recording error. Fish in the FishBase freshwater environment class with a native or endemic status count. Diadromous species are excluded because they cross seas.

dataset.name: FishBase
dataset.why_it_fits: FishBase has country checklists with status flags (native, endemic, introduced) and an ecology field that separates freshwater from brackish and marine species. These fields are used to build continent-level species lists and count overlaps.
